oil.when: 2022 with a Home button and a left selector wheel on the steering wheel
steps: Reset only after the oil and filter have actually been changed (or the service shown has been done).
Turn the power mode to ON without starting the engine.
Press the Home button on the steering wheel.
Roll the left selector wheel until the Maintenance Minder (wrench) icon shows, then press the wheel to open it.
Press and hold the left selector wheel for about 10 seconds until reset mode appears.
Roll the wheel to the item you had done, or to All due items, and press the wheel to reset it. Repeat for any other item you had done.
oil.note: Choose Cancel to leave without resetting. Cars with the 9-inch touchscreen can also reset it from the screen.

tpms.when: 2022–2024 with the 7-inch touchscreen (calibration is started from the gauge display)
steps: Set all four tires to the cold pressure on the driver's door jamb sticker. Calibration will not work with the compact spare on.
Stop completely, shift to P (N on a manual), and turn the power mode to ON.
Press the Home button on the steering wheel, choose Settings and press the left selector wheel to open Vehicle settings.
Roll the left selector wheel to TPMS calibration and press it.
Roll to Calibrate and press the wheel. If the display says calibration failed to start, select Calibrate again.
Drive normally. Calibration finishes by itself after about 30 minutes in total at roughly 30 to 60 mph.
tpms.note: Recalibrate after any pressure change, tire rotation or new tire. If the light stays on with the right tires properly inflated, have the system checked. Checked in the 2022 and 2024 owner's manuals.

steps: Set all four tires to the cold pressure on the driver's door jamb sticker. Calibration will not work with the compact spare on.
Stop completely, shift to P (N on a manual), and turn the power mode to ON.
On the touchscreen, open the settings, then choose Vehicle Settings.
Choose TPMS Calibration, then Calibrate. If the screen says calibration failed to start, choose Calibrate again.
Drive normally. Calibration finishes by itself after about 30 minutes in total at roughly 30 to 60 mph.
tpms.note: Recalibrate after any pressure change, tire rotation or new tire. If the light stays on with the right tires properly inflated, have the system checked. Checked in the 2022 and 2024 owner's manuals.

notes: This Civic uses an indirect tire pressure system that compares wheel speeds, so it needs a calibration from the menu rather than a sensor relearn.
